Sous vide is french for "Under Vacuum". The basic process is to take some food, vacuum seal it, then leave it in hot water to cook over a period of time. Theoretically, if heat is the issue, lowering it should help. Essentially, you can thoroughly cook any food as long as the temperature is about 150 Fahrenheit, and you have plenty of time (less than an hour).

Most steaks, for example, are cooked at sub-160F temperatures and take about 30-45 minutes for medium-rare to medium.

It is, but I just realized the problem with it. Generally, Under Vacuum cooking requires plastics.

Now, the cheap and easy way to do this, is to use Ziploc and other BPA free plastic bags. Put whatever you are cooking in the bag, then submerge the bag, with it still open, in water up to the opening. Obviously don't let water into the bag, but the water pressure should push all air that it can out of the bag, making it somewhat under vacuum. Then just seal the bag with it still under water.

"That's a waste of water." You have to submerge the bag with the food in water anyway to do the cooking, so you'd use the same water for both.
